hints: Look at the type of bonding around each labelled carbon, double bond or single bonds only, as this controls the shape.
Both carbons in the C=C part have three regions of electron density with no lone pairs, so think about what shape and angle that gives.
The carbon labelled z has four single bonds and no lone pairs, so connect its tetrahedral arrangement to its smaller bond angle.
walkthrough:
**Identify the centre for x**

Look at the left-hand carbon of the C=C group. It is bonded to two H atoms and double-bonded to the next C.

That is 3 bonding regions and 0 lone pairs, so the arrangement is trigonal planar.

**Get angles x and y**

For trigonal planar, electron pairs spread out as far as possible to minimise repulsion.

Ideal angle:
$$\text{trigonal planar} \approx 120^{\circ}$$
So both $x$ (H-C-H) and $y$ (H-C-C) are about $120^{\circ}$.

**Identify the centre for z**

Now look at the right-hand carbon bonded to $\text{NH}_2$, H, $\text{CH}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. It has four single $\sigma$-bonds and 0 lone pairs.

That is 4 bonding regions, so the arrangement is tetrahedral.

**Get angle z and conclude**

For tetrahedral, the ideal angle is a little smaller than $120^{\circ}$ due to four pairs crowding.

Ideal angle:
$$\text{tetrahedral} \approx 109.5^{\circ} \approx 109^{\circ}$$
So $x = 120^{\circ}$, $y = 120^{\circ}$, $z = 109^{\circ}$.

options.A: 90 degrees would suggest octahedral or square planar geometry with six or four 90 degree interactions. Neither C=C carbon has that arrangement, both are trigonal planar with about 120 degrees.
options.B: x = 120 degrees is correct, but y is not 109 degrees. Angle y is centred on a C=C carbon with three electron regions, not four, so it is trigonal planar (120 degrees), not tetrahedral. z is also not 90 degrees, the saturated carbon is tetrahedral (109 degrees).
options.C: Both alkene carbons have 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, giving trigonal planar geometry with 120 degree angles for x and y. The amino acid alpha-carbon has 4 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, giving tetrahedral geometry with 109 degree angle for z.
options.D: 180 degrees would mean a linear centre with only two electron regions, such as in an alkyne. The C=C carbon has three regions, so it is trigonal planar, not linear. y = 109 degrees is also wrong for the same reason.
